findings.title: Ability checks OR ruler and Prometheus results, widening permissions
findings.body: canPause, canDelete, canDuplicate, canSilence, and canExport are each true if either the ruler-rule ability or the Grafana Prometheus ability allows the action. Callers that still have a ruler rule (rule detail and any menu that passes both) previously trusted only the ruler check. The Prometheus path treats a rule as not provisioned when provenance is missing, and it never treats groups as federated, so a denial from the ruler check can be overridden and Edit, Delete, Pause, Duplicate, Silence, or Export can appear for provisioned or otherwise immutable rules. These flags should fall back to the Prometheus abilities only when rulerRule is absent, not be unioned.

findings.title: Edit button uses the same permissive OR of ability checks
findings.body: canEditRule is true when either useRulerRuleAbility or useGrafanaPromRuleAbility allows Update. Any caller that still passes a ruler rule plus a Grafana prom rule (the previous V2 contract always had a ruler rule) can now show Edit even when the ruler result says the rule is not editable, for example a provisioned rule whose Prometheus DTO has no provenance. Use the Prometheus result only as a fallback when rule is undefined.

findings.title: Delete and Pause never render in the ruler-free list
findings.body: The list view now passes only promRule into AlertRuleMenu, and canDelete/canPause can be true from the new Prometheus abilities. The Delete item is still gated on rulerRule (line 165) and Pause is still gated on rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule) (line 123), and both handlers require a RulerRuleDTO. With no ruler payload those actions are impossible to open, so users lose Delete and Pause from the alert list even when folder permissions allow them. RuleActionsButtons already builds an identifier and delete modal from the Prometheus uid, so the menu gate is what blocks delete. GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx grants AlertingRuleDelete, defines a delete menu selector, and then asserts exactly four items (silence, copy link, duplicate, export), which locks this regression in.

findings.title: Silence menu item is a no-op without a ruler rule
findings.body: List rows render RuleActionsButtons with only promRule. AlertRuleMenu can still show Silence notifications because canSilence is taken from the Prometheus ability, and handleSilence only sets showSilenceDrawer. The drawer is rendered only when rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) is true, so in the list view the click never opens SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer. Users with silence permission get a menu action that does nothing.

findings.title: Federated rule groups are no longer treated as immutable
findings.body: useAllAlertRuleAbilities used to set isFederated from isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group) (source_tenants) and fold that into immutableRule, which disables update, delete, pause, restore, and permanent delete. The refactored useAllRulerRuleAbilities hardcodes isFederated to false with a TODO, and every combined-rule and ruler-rule ability check now goes through it. Federated cloud rules therefore show edit and delete actions they were previously blocked from, and the backend may reject the write or apply it in the wrong tenant scope.

findings.title: Recording rules lose export, pause, restore, and permanent delete
findings.body: useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities sets ModifyExport, Pause, Restore, and DeletePermanently from isAlertingRule (prometheus type alerting). The ruler implementation used isGrafanaManagedAlertRule, which includes Grafana recording rules. Silence correctly needs an alerting rule, but the other four actions were not limited that way. On the new list, which only consults this hook, Grafana recording rules no longer get Export (and will not get Pause once that item no longer requires a ruler rule), even though they are Grafana-managed and still editable.

findings.title: Filtered Grafana rules are rendered without a React key
findings.body: Switching the filtered list from GrafanaRuleLoader to GrafanaRuleListItem dropped key={key} on the grafana branch of the map. Datasource rows still use the stable key computed by getRuleKey. Filter results are appended as the user scrolls, so missing keys make React reuse the wrong row state (open menus, action buttons) across different rules and can show the wrong rule's actions after the next page loads.

findings.title: Rule view links no longer include returnTo
findings.body: The removed list item built the view href with createReturnTo() so Back from the rule page returned to the current list, including filters. The new href is createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`) with no returnTo query. From the filtered list, opening a rule and going back lands on the default alerting page instead of the filtered results.
